## How a table is built — every part explained

A table has **3 layers of nesting**. Read from outside in:

```
<table>        ← the whole table
  <thead>      ← the header section (top row with column names)
    <tr>       ← one row
      <th>     ← one header cell (bold by default)
  <tbody>      ← the body section (the actual data rows)
    <tr>       ← one row
      <td>     ← one data cell
```

---

### `<table border="1">`
Creates the table. `border="1"` adds a visible border line — without it the table has no lines and looks invisible. Later we will do this with CSS instead (cleaner).

### `<thead>` and `<tbody>`
These split the table into two sections:
- `<thead>` — the top row with column titles (Invoice, Product, etc.)
- `<tbody>` — all the actual data rows below it

The browser uses this split to do useful things — like keeping the header visible when you scroll a long list.

### `<tr>` — Table Row
Every horizontal row is wrapped in `<tr>`. You add as many `<tr>` blocks as you have rows of data.

### `<th>` vs `<td>`
- `<th>` = **t**able **h**eader cell — bold, used in `<thead>`
- `<td>` = **t**able **d**ata cell — normal text, used in `<tbody>`

---

## The pattern to remember

Every row `<tr>` must have the **same number of cells** as the header. Our header has 4 `<th>` cells, so every data row must have 4 `<td>` cells. If they don't match, the columns break.

`django-admin` is Django's setup tool. `startproject` means "create a new project and name it this".

---

### Command 3 — Create the app
```
cd tramed_app
python manage.py startapp pharmacy
```
This created the `pharmacy/` folder:
```
pharmacy/
├── models.py    ← created by this command
├── views.py     ← created by this command
├── admin.py     ← created by this command
└── apps.py      ← created by this command
```

---

## The difference between a project and an app

This confuses everyone at first:

| | Project (`tramed_app`) | App (`pharmacy`) |
|---|---|---|
| **What it is** | The whole website | One feature/section of the website |
| **How many** | One per website | As many as you need |
| **Contains** | Settings, URL map | Models, views, templates |
| **Analogy** | The whole pharmacy building | One department inside it |

A big project can have many apps — for example you could later have a `pharmacy` app, a `users` app, a `reports` app. Each handles its own section.

## What each file does — the ones that matter

### `manage.py`
Your **command centre**. You never edit this file — you just use it to run commands:
```
python manage.py runserver      ← starts the server
python manage.py migrate        ← updates the database
python manage.py createsuperuser ← creates an admin login
```

### `settings.py`
**Configuration** for the whole project — database type, installed apps, language, timezone. Think of it as the pharmacy's operating rules.

### `urls.py`
The **URL map** — tells Django which URL goes to which page:
```python

path('sales/', views.sales)           ← /sales → show sales page

### `views.py` ← we build here after
Contains the **logic for each page**. When someone visits `/dashboard`, a view runs, fetches data from the database, and sends it to the HTML template.
